title: Composition isomorphism for $Lf^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
For morphisms $f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$ of the setting and a commutative condensed
ring $\Lambda$, the *composition isomorphism*

$$
L(g\circ f)^*\cong Lf^*\circ Lg^*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)
$$

of the restricted pullbacks of [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] is the unique natural isomorphism whose
image under the inclusion into $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is the ambient composition isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct the ambient comparison on the same module-object categories as the item. Write $L_h$ for the ambient $Lh^*$. Abelian sheaves are sheaves of modules over the constant integer sheaf: on constant integer sections the action is repeated addition, and sections of the sheafified constant integer presheaf act by gluing these local actions. The sheaf gluing axiom gives existence and uniqueness of this action, so it adds no data to an abelian sheaf or its morphisms. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] these sheaf categories are abelian; in particular equalizers and coequalizers are kernels and cokernels of differences. For $h=f,g,g\circ f$, [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives $h^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_h}\operatorname{mapMod}(h^*_{\Ab})$ with $\alpha_h$ invertible. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact] with coefficient category $\Ab$ to obtain exactness of $h^*_{\Ab}$. The sheaf tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] is closed symmetric monoidal and right exact in each variable. Each tensor functor preserves finite coproducts; between abelian categories this implies additivity, since addition of maps is expressed using diagonal and codiagonal maps of biproducts. Hence the tensor hypotheses of [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] hold for the coefficient rings $\Lambda_S$, $h^*\Lambda_S$ and $\Lambda_T$, where $h:T\to S$. By [sk-def-sfb-transport] (1), $\operatorname{mapMod}(h^*_{\Ab})$ commutes with forgetful functors, so the lifting lemma with $F=h^*_{\Ab}$ makes it exact. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] (4)--(5), $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_h}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_h^{-1}}$ and this restriction is exact. Its hypotheses hold because the abelian sheaf categories have equalizers and coequalizers and their closed symmetric tensor preserves colimits. Thus $h^*$, a composite of exact functors, is exact. Thus [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], Exact functors, identifies $L_h$ with $D(h^*)$, the functor induced termwise; these termwise functors therefore invert quasi-isomorphisms. Let $a:(g\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*g^*$ be [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. On a complex $K^\bullet$ use $a_{K^n}$ in degree $n$: naturality of $a$ with respect to $d^n$ makes this a chain isomorphism, and naturality with respect to each degree of a complex map makes it a natural isomorphism of complex functors. Localize it in the target. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) with source the complexes of $\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}$, $W$ the quasi-isomorphisms, localization $Q_Z$, and target $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$. Take the two descended functors to be $L_{g\circ f}$ and $L_fL_g$, using their exact-functor termwise comparisons. For $h:T\to S$ write $\psi_h:L_hQ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_T\operatorname{CoCh}(h^*)$ for its canonical exact-functor comparison. Set $\phi_1=\psi_{g\circ f}$ and $\phi_{2,K}=\psi_{f,\operatorname{CoCh}(g^*)K}\circ L_f(\psi_{g,K})$, so $\phi_2:L_fL_gQ_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_X\operatorname{CoCh}(f^*g^*)$. Then descent gives the unique $c:L_{g\circ f}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_fL_g$ satisfying $c_{Q_ZK}=\phi_{2,K}^{-1}\circ Q_X(a_{K^\bullet})\circ\phi_{1,K}$. Its inverse is the descent of $a^{-1}$, since descent preserves compositions and identities. This is precisely the ambient composition comparison, normalized by the ordinary module pullback comparison on complexes.

source.place: Clause 4 using clause 3; exactness expanded by det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main.proof.md, Setting, Transport, Extension of scalars and Conclusion; descent of transformations by the cited localization node (Stacks 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, for functor descent).

proof.text:
Write $L_h^c$ for the restricted functors and $\iota_T:D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)\hookrightarrow D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ for the inclusions. By [def-sfb-dc-upper-star], for $h:T\to S$ the restriction comes with its inclusion comparison $e_h:\iota_TL_h^c\xrightarrow{\sim}L_h\iota_S$ (an equality in the strict restriction model). Paste these comparisons with $c$ from step 1 to obtain
$$A:\iota_XL_{g\circ f}^c\xrightarrow{e_{g\circ f}}L_{g\circ f}\iota_Z\xrightarrow{c\iota_Z}L_fL_g\iota_Z\xrightarrow{L_fe_g^{-1}}L_f\iota_YL_g^c\xrightarrow{e_f^{-1}L_g^c}\iota_XL_f^cL_g^c.$$
Each arrow is a natural isomorphism, so their componentwise composite is one. All objects lie in the indicated domains because the restricted pullbacks of the cited definition are defined for every morphism of the setting and every commutative condensed $\Lambda$.

By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], morphisms between bounded constructible objects are exactly their ambient derived morphisms, with the same identities and composition. For each $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$ define $c^c_K:L_{g\circ f}^cK\to L_f^cL_g^cK$ to be the very morphism $A_K$, now read in this full subcategory; define its inverse to be $A_K^{-1}$ in the same way. The two inverse equations hold because their images are the ambient inverse equations and the Hom sets are unchanged. For every $u:K\to K'$, the naturality equation for these components is exactly the naturality equation for $A$ on $u$ in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$, again in the same Hom set. Hence $c^c$ is a natural isomorphism and its image under $\iota_X$ is $A$.

If $b$ is another natural isomorphism with the specified ambient image, then for every $K$ its component $b_K$ and $c^c_K$ have the same image $A_K$. The inclusion is the identity on the Hom sets by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], so $b_K=c^c_K$ for every $K$; componentwise equality gives $b=c^c$. Define the composition isomorphism to be $c^c$. Under the inclusion comparisons $e_h$ of step 2 its ambient image is $c$ of step 1, exactly as required.

No new nodes and no assertion that the upstream master construction is finished. Second reading supplies the omitted exactness citations and checks their tensor and scalar-change hypotheses; the localized component formula fixes the ambient normalization explicitly. Fresh second reading also cites the abelian-sheaf category structure and corrects the domain of the step-3 naturality check. Current independent reading spells out the constant-integer sheaf action by gluing and tensor additivity from finite coproduct preservation, and rechecks all thirteen citation pairs.
